githubactions:S6505.name: JavaScript package manager scripts should not be executed during installation
githubactions:S6505.why: Package installation can execute lifecycle scripts supplied by dependencies.
githubactions:S6505.risks: A compromised dependency can run code with the build process permissions and expose credentials or alter artifacts.
githubactions:S6505.remediation: Review whether installation scripts are needed and use the package manager controls that disable unaudited scripts; test required build functionality afterwards.

csharpsquid:S2068.name: Credentials should not be hard-coded
csharpsquid:S2068.why: Credentials embedded in code or connection strings are distributed with the source or application.
csharpsquid:S2068.risks: Readers of a repository, build artifact or backup may obtain access to the associated service.
csharpsquid:S2068.remediation: Move credentials to an appropriate protected configuration or secrets service. Rotate any genuinely exposed credential; moving it alone does not revoke it.

secrets:S6698.name: PostgreSQL database passwords should not be disclosed
secrets:S6698.why: The rule identifies a PostgreSQL password in source.
secrets:S6698.risks: A disclosed database password may permit unauthorized access according to the account permissions and network exposure.
secrets:S6698.remediation: Revoke or change exposed credentials, remove the value from uncontrolled distribution and use a protected secret source. Verify the real affected account and context.

csharpsquid:S4790.name: Weak hashing algorithms should not be used
csharpsquid:S4790.why: Weak or unsuitable hashes can undermine the purpose of protecting sensitive data.
csharpsquid:S4790.risks: Password hashes may permit inexpensive guessing, while weak hashes used for integrity may permit substitution attacks. The exact impact depends on use.
csharpsquid:S4790.remediation: Use a suitable password KDF for password storage, and modern cryptographic hashes for appropriate non-password integrity uses; choose and verify settings for the use case.

csharpsquid:S3330.name: Cookies should have the "HttpOnly" flag
csharpsquid:S3330.why: A cookie without HttpOnly can be read by scripts in the page context.
csharpsquid:S3330.risks: If an XSS path exists, a script-readable session cookie can be stolen and used for impersonation.
csharpsquid:S3330.remediation: Enable HttpOnly for sensitive cookies and verify actual Set-Cookie behavior. This control does not itself remove XSS or stop every authenticated action from an injected script.

csharpsquid:S2092.name: Cookies should have the "secure" flag
csharpsquid:S2092.why: A cookie without Secure can be transmitted over an unencrypted HTTP connection.
csharpsquid:S2092.risks: An attacker able to observe that connection may obtain a sensitive cookie.
csharpsquid:S2092.remediation: Use Secure for sensitive cookies over HTTPS and validate transport behavior. Account for the actual deployment and the intentionally plain-HTTP training environment when planning a change.

csharpsquid:S2077.name: SQL queries should not be dynamically formatted
csharpsquid:S2077.why: Building SQL by formatting or concatenating values can let data alter query syntax.
csharpsquid:S2077.risks: Untrusted values may change a database operation or expose data; inspection of the surrounding input and authorization checks is still required.
csharpsquid:S2077.remediation: Bind values through the database API parameters and review any dynamic identifiers against a controlled mapping. Verify intended queries and negative cases.

roslyn.sonaranalyzer.security.cs:S5144.name: Server-side requests should not be vulnerable to forging attacks
roslyn.sonaranalyzer.security.cs:S5144.why: An attacker-controlled destination can cause a server to make requests on the attacker’s behalf.
roslyn.sonaranalyzer.security.cs:S5144.risks: Depending on reachable services and returned data, SSRF can disclose information or trigger unauthorized actions. Rule context alone does not prove reachability.
roslyn.sonaranalyzer.security.cs:S5144.remediation: Constrain destinations and protocols to the business requirement, validate redirects and resolution, and use network controls. Verify allowed and rejected requests using authorized targets.

docker:S6505.name: JavaScript package manager scripts should not be executed during installation
docker:S6505.why: Package installation can execute lifecycle scripts supplied by dependencies.
docker:S6505.risks: A compromised dependency can run code with the build process permissions and expose credentials or alter artifacts.
docker:S6505.remediation: Review whether installation scripts are needed and use the package manager controls that disable unaudited scripts; test required build functionality afterwards.

typescript:S5332.name: Clear-text protocols should not be used
typescript:S5332.why: Clear-text protocols do not protect traffic in transit.
typescript:S5332.risks: An observer or active network attacker may read or modify data; the risk depends on the actual network and transported information.
typescript:S5332.remediation: Use an encrypted transport suitable for the service and verify the deployed connection. Internal development HTTP and production exposure must be assessed separately.
